in_hebrew.name: Hymen
in_hebrew.long_meaning: Hymen הוא שם נוצרי עם משמעות רוחנית עמוקה בתרבות הנצרות. From Greek hymenos, hymen, threshold, door, or wedding veil. In ancient Greek culture, a bride would step over a hymen, a threshold or veil, to symbolize the transition to married life. In Christianity, the hymen is a symbol of purity and innocence, particularly associated with the Virgin Mary.

in_greek.name: Ὑμεν
in_greek.long_meaning: From the ancient Greek word 'ὑμνέω' (hymneō) which means 'to sing a hymn, to make a vow, to swear an oath, to celebrate a wedding, or to make a covenant'. In ancient Greek culture, Hymen was the god of marriage and was invoked during weddings to ensure a successful union. The veil worn by the bride during the wedding ceremony was also called a 'hymen' and symbolized the bride's virginity.
